name: auth-core
task: OAuth and OIDC sign-in without a vendor
what: headless auth protocol engine behind auth.js: provider definitions; PKCE; token exchange; JWT or database sessions; adapters for common ORMs
adoption: 7.2M dl/wk (0.41.3 - published 2026-07-20; next-auth stable still 4.24.15 with 5.0.0-beta.32 on beta)
excels: wiring many OAuth providers correctly exactly once
why: provider quirks (state; nonce; scope drift; clock skew) are already solved and audited instead of re-implemented per app
when_to_use: Express or Fastify or SvelteKit or Astro apps that want auth.js semantics and keep tokens in your own database
when_not: check the release train: the v5 line still ships as beta while next-auth latest is 4.24.15 so expect migration churn; better-auth when you also need 2FA and orgs and user admin; passport for niche SAML or CAS providers

name: better-auth
what: framework-agnostic TypeScript auth library owning its own tables; CLI; plugins for 2FA; organizations; passkeys; JWT; multi-session; admin
excels: owning auth in your own database with a typed API and no per-user bill
why: replaces the session and token and cookie and OTP code every backend re-derives; it is also where lucia users are pointed - lucia 3.2.2 is npm-deprecated (verified deprecation notice; 0.72M dl/wk residual) so no new work should start there
when_to_use: new products needing email plus OAuth plus 2FA while keeping data and cost under your control
when_not: a managed IdP (@auth/core or a commercial provider) for enterprise SSO and SCIM; the 1.x surface moves fast so pin versions and read changelogs; passport only for legacy strategy catalogs

name: bullmq
what: Redis-backed queue system: workers; priorities; delayed and repeatable jobs; rate limits; flows (DAG dependencies); progress events
excels: at-least-once job processing with concurrency and retry semantics across many workers
why: job claiming is atomic Redis Lua so a crashed worker cannot lose or double-run work you would otherwise hand-recover
when_to_use: production fan-out (emails; transcoding; webhook delivery; imports) with several worker processes and a dashboard
when_not: no Redis in the stack - pg-boss keeps jobs transactional in Postgres; a single in-process timer is just setTimeout; process supervision is not job work (pm2 3.9M dl/wk - AGPL-3.0 since v7 - or the container runtime owns restarts)

name: croner
what: zero-dependency cron parser and scheduler: 5 and 6-field expressions; patterns like every monday; timezone and DST aware; next-run math
excels: running a schedule inside one process with no dependencies and no scheduler service
why: correct DST and missed-run handling is subtle; the setInterval cron you write is wrong twice a year
when_to_use: housekeeping you would otherwise hand-roll: nightly cleanup; polling jobs; scheduled reports
when_not: replicas that must not all fire the same job - use bullmq repeatable jobs or pg-boss so one worker wins; node-cron (6.8M dl/wk) for API familiarity; cron (9.3M dl/wk) for its parser and second-level fields

name: drizzle-orm
what: TypeScript SQL mapper: schema-as-code; SQL-like builder; relational queries across Postgres MySQL SQLite SQL Server and D1; drizzle-kit (42.4M dl/wk) diffs and generates migration SQL
excels: staying close to SQL while every column and join stays typed
why: you keep the database you already run and migration files stay plain readable SQL rather than an opaque engine output
when_to_use: teams writing SQL-shaped code who want one schema source for queries and migrations; serverless cold starts favor the lighter runtime
when_not: prisma when the team wants a schema DSL and generated client over hand-written queries; for migrations only use node-pg-migrate (1.3M dl/wk) or umzug (3.2M dl/wk); always review generated destructive diffs

name: keyv
what: namespaced get/set with TTL over Memory; Redis (@keyv/redis 2.1M dl/wk); Postgres; SQLite; file stores - with serialization and stats events
excels: caching behind one API so the backing store becomes a config choice
why: switching Redis for Postgres or memory should not touch call sites; the events give you hit and miss metrics for free
when_to_use: application-level cache-through: session fragments; expensive renders; upstream API responses with per-key TTL
when_not: raw redis (20.4M dl/wk) when you need pipelines; transactions; sorted sets; streams or pub-sub - Keyv is key-value plus TTL only; and a plain Map is enough for one short-lived process cache

name: multer
what: Express-compatible middleware over busboy (43M dl/wk) for memory or disk storage with size and file-count limits and per-field handling
adoption: 30.4M dl/wk (2.5.0 - released 2026-10-22; the 2.x line closed the 1.x DoS advisories)
excels: bounded and validated upload handling inside middleware
why: boundary parsing is a quoting and charset state machine with overflow paths - hand-rolled versions get DoS-ed and leak temporary files
when_to_use: form uploads behind Express where you want enforced limits and a storage choice in one place
when_not: presign direct-to-S3 or R2 for large or user-facing media so your bandwidth and disk are not the bottleneck; stream with busboy or a framework-native multipart plugin when you must process without touching disk; note cors (122.8M dl/wk) and compression (60.1M dl/wk) are one-line middleware rather than decisions

name: nodemailer
what: mature mail composer plus transports: pooled SMTP; OAuth2; DKIM signing; SES-style HTTP backends; offline test mode
excels: sending through any provider or your own relay with zero vendor lock
why: MIME construction and connection pooling are quietly hard; it has been hardened for years and MIT-0 removes license questions
when_to_use: self-hosted or bring-your-own-provider mail; bulk sending over pooled connections; local dev capture with no bill and no sandbox key
when_not: resend or any API vendor when you do not want to own deliverability and bounce handling; never send production mail from a hobby IP because in this model the reputation problem is yours

name: openapi-typescript
task: OpenAPI codegen for types and clients
what: generates TypeScript types from an OpenAPI 3 document; orval (3.7M dl/wk; 8.47.0) turns the same spec into typed fetch or axios or react-query clients plus mocks
excels: keeping hand-written HTTP calls honest to the published contract
why: types derived from the spec cannot drift the way parallel hand-written interfaces do
when_to_use: consuming a third-party or in-house REST API that ships OpenAPI; add orval when the request functions and mock handlers should be generated too
when_not: @trpc/server when both ends are TypeScript inside your own repo - codegen there is ceremony you can delete; GraphQL servers generate types from the schema instead; hand-written types are acceptable for three calls

name: passport
what: middleware that delegates to numbered strategies (local; OAuth1 and OAuth2; SAML) and repopulates req.user from a serialized session
excels: a huge catalog of identity-provider strategies
why: nothing else covers an obscure SAML or CAS or OAuth1 provider with a package somebody already published and maintained
when_to_use: existing Express apps already wired to passport - keep it working; also the pragmatic route for a legacy enterprise IdP
when_not: new projects: better-auth (19.1M dl/wk; published today) and @auth/core are actively released and typed; the serialize and deserialize plus req.login ceremony is the boilerplate newer libraries deleted

name: pg-boss
what: job queues; delayed jobs; cron-style scheduling; retries and dead-letter history tables - all stored in Postgres on advisory locks
excels: jobs that commit atomically with the rows they describe
why: inserting the job in the same transaction as the business row removes the dual-write window that hand-rolled queues get wrong
when_to_use: you already run Postgres; volume is thousands not millions an hour; you want queues and cron without operating Redis
when_not: bullmq when you need flows; priorities; dashboards; or Redis-level throughput; keep payloads small and store blobs in object storage by reference; no built-in UI

name: pino
what: fast JSON-line logger with levels and serializers; pino-pretty (34.9M dl/wk) adds the colored dev transport
excels: near-zero overhead structured logs on hot paths
why: one JSON line per request with bound ids beats console.log strings you cannot query later; redaction strips secrets out of payload objects
when_to_use: any Node or Bun server whose logs reach a collector; run the pretty transport in dev only
when_not: winston when infra demands its transports or human-readable non-JSON files; plain console for throwaway CLIs

name: prisma
task: ORM with schema DSL client and migrate
what: schema.prisma plus a generated typed client; Prisma Migrate with shadow-database diffing; query compiler and first-party Postgres offer (stable @prisma/client 7.10.1 while the latest tag sits on an 8.0.0 RC)
excels: the shortest path from a schema to typed CRUD with migrations
why: it removes the repository plumbing and gives editor-visible relation types that hand-written SQL layers make you test for
when_to_use: product teams shipping form-heavy CRUD where owning emitted SQL is not a priority; apps wanting hooks and one schema across services
when_not: drizzle-orm when you must own SQL and readable migration files or trim generated artifacts and build steps; add npx prisma generate to CI and pin 7.x because the 8 line is not stable yet

name: rate-limiter-flexible
what: atomic limiters with in-memory; Redis; MySQL; PostgreSQL; MongoDB stores plus memory-blocklist and fail-at-first-request options
excels: correct distributed counters under concurrent requests
why: check-and-increment must be atomic; it ships the Lua and pipeline code so you never write the racing version yourself
when_to_use: login and signup attempt limits; per-IP or per-API-key quotas; burst protection with penalty blocks
when_not: put limits at the edge (gateway; CDN; nginx; Envoy) when you already have one - far cheaper per request; a Map suffices in one process; throttling background work belongs to bullmq

name: resend
what: official Node SDK for the Resend email API: send; batch; domains; attachments; pairs with React Email templates
excels: deliverability and send logs without running or trusting an SMTP path
why: the vendor owns SPF and DKIM and IP reputation and returns webhooks for bounces instead of you inferring them
when_to_use: new product email where accepting a vendor is cheaper than owning reputation; serverless runtimes where SMTP ports are blocked
when_not: nodemailer when you must relay through your own SES or Postfix or Google Workspace or avoid per-mail pricing; marketing campaigns belong to an ESP; data-residency rules can rule the SaaS out

name: sentry-node
what: official Node SDK built on OpenTelemetry spans: exception capture; breadcrumbs; performance traces; HTTP and DB integrations; releases and source maps
excels: finding the exception and the slow trace behind it in one place
why: source-map symbolication; issue grouping; sampling and release tagging are never finished when you hand-roll them
when_to_use: any production server where an uncaught error must page someone with context; pair it with pino so logs and traces correlate
when_not: @opentelemetry/api (142.2M dl/wk) plus a vendor-neutral backend when telemetry must not lock to one vendor or OTel already spans your services; self-hosted Sentry is an ops commitment you are choosing

name: socket-io
task: realtime channels with rooms and reconnect
what: ws-based protocol with namespaces; rooms; typed events; acknowledgements; automatic reconnection; HTTP long-poll fallback; Redis adapter for multi-node
excels: browser sockets that survive proxies and flaky networks
why: reconnect with state resync; per-room broadcast; and delivery acknowledgements are tedious and buggy over raw ws
when_to_use: interactive multi-user UI (chat; collaboration; live dashboards) served by several nodes - add the Redis adapter and let the client handle resumption
when_not: two-way sockets are wrong for one-way updates - use SSE or polling; server-to-server or native mobile clients should speak plain ws; the client bundle plus handshake is real overhead

name: stripe
what: official Node SDK for the Stripe REST API: typed resources; idempotency keys; webhook signature verification; classified errors (v23.1.0; engines node>=20)
excels: checkout; subscriptions; invoices; refunds and payouts from code without hand-rolling REST
why: it keeps card data out of your scope through tokenization and gives webhook HMAC verification plus API version pinning - both unsafe to write yourself
when_to_use: any server-side billing: payment intents; subscription lifecycle; event ingestion; reconciliation
when_not: it is a vendor SDK not a payment strategy - confirm regional coverage and fees first; merchant-of-record resellers change the tax model entirely; webhook handlers must be idempotent whatever you pick
alternatives: gateway REST via native fetch;local PSP SDKs

name: t3-oss-env-core
what: runtime env validation bound to any schema library (zod; Valibot; ArkType) with client/server key split and inferred types; @t3-oss/env-nextjs 3.6M dl/wk wraps it
excels: making process.env typed and failing loudly at boot
why: a missing or malformed variable should crash startup rather than surface as a 500 at 3am; one typed object across every entrypoint
when_to_use: servers with more than a handful of env vars; monorepos sharing config between web and worker packages
when_not: dotenv (258.5M dl/wk) when you only need loading with no validation - and Node 20+ --env-file plus Bun and Deno load .env natively so the loader may need no package at all; bare process.env reads for tiny CLIs

name: trpc-server
task: typed internal API between your TS client and server
what: server procedures callable from a typed client with end-to-end inference; v11 adapters for plain Node http; Express; Fastify; AWS Lambda; plus Bun and Deno
excels: deleting the fetch-and-cast layer inside one TypeScript codebase
why: one import graph means the client stops compiling when the server signature changes - no contract file left to forget
when_to_use: monorepos where you own both ends and every consumer is TypeScript: admin panels and first-party web apps
when_not: public or third-party APIs need REST plus OpenAPI (openapi-typescript) or GraphQL - graphql-yoga (3.0M dl/wk; mercurius 0.32M dl/wk when the host is Fastify); non-TS clients and heavy streaming belong on other channels

name: winston
what: multi-transport logger (rotating files; syslog; remote sinks) with custom formatters and child loggers
excels: tee-ing one log stream into several heterogeneous sinks
why: its transport ecosystem predates structured logging so the legacy sink you are told to write to already has one
when_to_use: ops contracts that name specific transports or want non-JSON output; reusing an existing approved winston config
when_not: pino for throughput and JSON discipline - winston costs more per line and its transport layer hides backpressure; 3.19.0 (Dec 2025) is a slow train next to pino 10.4.0 (Oct 2026)

name: ws
what: spec-complete W3C WebSocket implementation for Node with upgrade control; permessage-deflate; ping-pong and bufferedAmount backpressure signals
excels: being the transport other libraries and your own protocol build on
why: the smallest surface that gets the protocol right (fragmentation; close handshake; flow control) - socket.io rides it through engine.io
when_to_use: your own message protocol: presence; live activity; collaborative or trading streams where you must control the handshake and headers
when_not: socket.io when you want rooms and acknowledgements and reconnect with long-poll fallback; SSE or polling for one-way server-to-browser feeds; Bun and Deno expose native WebSocket servers

name: liveline
what: real-time line charts
excels: time-scrolling live data
why: streaming datasets break static chart libs
when_to_use: live dashboards
when_not: static dashboards (recharts)

name: recharts
what: declarative chart kit
excels: dashboards fast
why: standard charts without d3 plumbing
when_to_use: 90% of dashboard needs
when_not: streaming (liveline); custom viz (visx)

name: clack-prompts
what: small prompt kit (text select multiselect confirm spinner group) with polished grouped step output and a tiny dependency footprint
excels: fewest lines per polished interactive flow in the ecosystem and it reached stable 1.x so the modern-gem label now has a version number behind it
why: verified as sane: only sisteransi @clack/core fast-wrap-ansi fast-string-width; active weekly releases; visually better defaults than the incumbent without pulling in React
when_to_use: install wizards scaffolding questions and short guided flows where you want the output to look designed
when_not: plain non-interactive CI is the trap - detect TTY and fall back to flags or env because prompts cannot render meaningfully without one; for long multi-step enterprise forms @inquirer/prompts 8.8.0 (61.6M downloads/wk; published 2026-11-10) is the deeper and better-tested prompt set
alternatives: inquirer @inquirer/prompts; enquirer; prompts; ink for full TUI

name: commander
task: CLI argument parsing and subcommand trees
what: declarative option and subcommand parser that generates help and handles errors exit codes and dotenv-style composition
runtime: Node 20+ for v15; ESM and CJS dual build
excels: zero dependencies plus the most familiar parsing semantics in the ecosystem so help output and exit behaviour are predictable and documented in the README alone
why: boring and enormously battle-tested; no runtime codegen and no decorator ceremony; pairs with any prompt or colour library
when_to_use: hand-written CLIs of moderate size; commands that must read identically to everyone else's; when you want no dependency tree
when_not: not typed-by-construction - you declare options and re-state types yourself; no built-in prompting (bring @clack/prompts or @inquirer/prompts) and no colouring (bring picocolors); yargs 18.2.0 (369.7M downloads/wk) brings auto-parsing and middleware machinery most CLIs never need and clipanion 4.0.0-rc.4 (6.3M downloads/wk; unchanged since 2024-09) is stuck in release candidates

name: ink
what: React renderer for the terminal: flexbox layout through yoga plus stdin and stdout handling so TUIs are components
excels: only mainstream way to build a live interactive terminal app with components state and hooks; verified React 19.3+ and Node 22+ peers plus chalk 6 inside
why: hand-rolled cursor movement and redraw logic breaks on resize and Windows terminals; ink owns layout and diffing
when_to_use: terminal dashboards live log viewers multi-field interactive wizards and anything that redraws continuously
when_not: overkill and a dependency tax for linear scripts: use ora 10.0.0 (129.5M downloads/wk) for spinners and progress and cli-table3 0.6.5 (47.4M downloads/wk; unmaintained since 2024-05) for tables; ESM-only plus Node 22 excludes older toolchains and it needs a real TTY
alternatives: @clack/prompts for guided prompts; blessed or blessed-style; plain ANSI writes; picocolors or chalk for styling

name: picocolors
what: minimal ANSI colour and style helpers with auto capability detection; no dependencies
runtime: any Node or Deno or Bun; terminal
excels: the honest tiny-wins row: real weight and cold-start savings only when you are shipping a dependency-free tool - its huge download count is mostly transitive (pulled in by vite and postcss and others) not chosen
why: one function per style and a tiny byte count; nothing to configure; colour support detection is good enough for pipes and CI
when_to_use: inside libraries and CLI frameworks where install size and startup are measured and you colour a dozen strings
when_not: no new maintenance since 2024-10 - API is small enough that done is defensible but do not expect fixes; application CLIs are better served by chalk 6.0.1 (620.8M downloads/wk; active) or ansis 4.5.0 (58.5M downloads/wk; published 2026-11-01; nested styles and HTML output and the closer match to chalk's API)

name: apollo-client
task: GraphQL client with normalized entity cache
what: Full GraphQL client: typed queries and fragments; InMemoryCache normalization; fetch policies; cursor pagination merge helpers; optimisticResponse; reactive variables for local state; link and SSR ecosystem
runtime: browser; Node; React Native; React bindings shipped in the same package
adoption: 8.2M npm dl/wk; 19.8k stars; v4.3.8 published 2026-11-09; repo pushed 2026-11-09
excels: Apps whose server boundary is a GraphQL schema where the same entities appear in many queries and screens
why: Entity dedup is the real win: one User updated by any mutation repaints everywhere - a query-key cache cannot do that over a normalized graph
when_to_use: Backend is GraphQL and you need fragments and codegen and cache merge policies and subscriptions inside one supported client
when_not: REST or tRPC or OpenAPI backends; small apps where codegen plus cache configuration cost more than they return - TanStack Query over graphql-request is lighter; HTTP polling only
alternatives: TanStack Query; urql; graphql-request; Relay; SWR plus manual cache

name: axios
what: Promise HTTP client for browser and Node: request and response interceptors; transform chain; upload and download progress events; AbortSignal cancellation; Node follow-redirects; wide adapter and plugin ecosystem
runtime: browsers; Node; React Native through adapters
adoption: 141.4M npm dl/wk; 109.4k stars; v1.21.1 published 2026-11-09; repo pushed 2026-11-11
excels: Enterprise API layers with cross-cutting policy: token refresh on 401; tracing headers; error mapping in one shared instance
why: The interceptor model is the mature answer to global request policy and mocks and SSR wrappers and query layers already integrate with it
when_to_use: You need upload or download progress or an existing axios plugin stack or a shared client doing auth refresh before any data layer
when_not: It is not a cache - pair it with TanStack Query instead of wrapping it in useState; new browser-only code can stay on fetch or ky; Node streaming and HTTP/2 tuning - got
alternatives: ky; ofetch; got; native fetch; axios-retry

name: conform
what: View adapter over DOM FormData and ConstraintValidation: useForm plus form.useInput; server-side parse with zod or standard-schema; reuses native HTML validation and error reporting; submits with no JavaScript; integrates with React Router actions and Remix and Next server actions
runtime: browsers plus any React 18 SSR runtime - React Router v7; Remix; Next server actions
adoption: 430k npm dl/wk; 2.6k stars; v1.21.3 published 2026-10-31; repo pushed 2026-11-11
excels: Forms that must submit successfully without JavaScript and share one validation schema between client and server
why: Native form submission stays the happy path so you delete the duplicate server-side validation layer agents otherwise forget to write
when_to_use: Router-driven SSR apps with server actions and login or settings forms that need no-JS operation and SEO-safe markup
when_not: Rich client-only interaction such as drag-sorting field arrays or live per-keystroke derived UI - react-hook-form or TanStack Form; non-React stacks need their own adapter
alternatives: react-hook-form; TanStack Form; zod alone; Remix validators; plain FormData
tags: forms; ssr; progressive-enhancement; validation; zod; formdata

name: fetch-event-source
what: Microsoft EventSource replacement built on fetch: POST and custom headers and body; resumable streaming with last-event-id; onopen onmessage onclose onerror callbacks; auto reconnect with retry control; tab-visibility pause handling
runtime: browsers only - relies on fetch plus ReadableStream; not Node
adoption: 5.6M npm dl/wk; 2.9k stars; v2.0.1 published 2021-04-25; repo pushed 2026-02-28
excels: Token-authenticated or POST-bodied SSE endpoints such as streamed LLM tokens and long-running job progress feeds
why: Native EventSource is GET-only with no headers so this is the de facto patch - most hand-written agent SSE loops re-derive exactly these reconnect rules
when_to_use: Browser consuming a server-sent-events feed that needs POST bodies and auth headers and controlled reconnection
when_not: Maintenance stalled at a 2021 release with open issues; Node consumers should drive eventsource-parser over fetch; full-duplex or fan-out needs a WebSocket vendor SDK; public GET-only feeds - native EventSource
alternatives: eventsource-parser; eventsource-client Ticket72 fork; native EventSource; pusher-js; ably

name: got
task: Node HTTP client with retry and timeouts and pagination
what: Human-friendly and powerful HTTP for Node: promises plus streams; retry configurable by amount and status and method and backoff; granular timeout categories; redirects and cookie handling; paginate helper; caching; HTTP/2; proxies and handlers
adoption: 50.6M npm dl/wk; 15.0k stars; v16.2.0 published 2026-10-30; repo pushed 2026-10-30
excels: Server-side outbound HTTP in services and CLIs and workers and scrapers where robustness matters more than client size
why: Retry policy and timeout budgets and pagination and redirect handling ship built and reviewed - exactly the loops an agent otherwise writes per integration
when_to_use: Node backend or tooling code that needs real HTTP controls including streams and proxy support
when_not: Any browser or React Native code - it does not run there; simple server-side calls - ofetch or native fetch suffices; long-lived bidirectional sockets - a WebSocket client
alternatives: ky; ofetch; undici; native fetch in Node; node-fetch legacy
tags: http; node; retry; timeout; streams; pagination

name: ky
task: fetch client with retry and timeout and pagination
what: Tiny HTTP client over the fetch API: throws HTTPError by default; retry with exponential backoff and jitter; timeout option; request and response hooks; JSON handling; extend instance composition; paginate helper following cursor or page links
runtime: browsers; Node 18+; Deno; Bun; Cloudflare Workers and other fetch runtimes
adoption: 9.4M npm dl/wk; 17.2k stars; v2.2.0 published 2026-10-09; repo pushed 2026-10-09
excels: API client modules where every call needs an auth header and a timeout and a retry policy and typed JSON without a framework
why: Replaces the hand-rolled attempt loop with sleep and the clearTimeout race - those become declarative options on one extended client instance
when_to_use: Building a typed API layer that sits under TanStack Query or SWR while keeping native fetch semantics in browser code
when_not: Node-only pipelines needing streams or proxies or HTTP/2 - got; upload and download progress with interceptor chains - axios; SSR async-context header propagation - ofetch
alternatives: got; ofetch; axios; native fetch plus p-retry; superagent

name: ofetch
task: isomorphic fetch with SSR-aware errors and retry
what: Unified fetch for Node and browser and workers from the unJS ecosystem: auto JSON; baseURL and query handling; retry and timeout options; interceptors; structured FetchError carrying statusCode plus parsed body; request-context-aware headers
runtime: Node; Bun; Deno; browsers; edge runtimes; Nitro and Nuxt internals
adoption: 26.4M npm dl/wk; 5.4k stars; v1.5.1 published 2025-11-01; repo pushed 2026-11-11
excels: Universal code in Nuxt or Nitro or Vite SSR where one call path must behave on server and client
why: Fixes the genuine isomorphic defect of global fetch headers leaking across SSR requests and returns errors that already carry the parsed response
when_to_use: You live in the Nuxt or Vite SSR world and want retry and timeout without a heavy client and one fetch abstraction everywhere
when_not: Browser React teams usually stay on ky or axios; advanced Node HTTP controls such as streams and proxies and HTTP/2 - got; response cache semantics belong in the data layer not the transport
alternatives: ky; axios; got; native fetch; axios-retry

name: p-retry
task: retry any async operation with backoff
what: Retries a promise-returning or async function: attempts; min and max timeout; factor-based exponential backoff; onFailedAttempt hook; abort by error message or class; AbortSignal support; makeRetriable wrapper helper
runtime: browsers; Node; Deno; Bun - ESM-only import
adoption: 69.4M npm dl/wk; 1.0k stars; v9.0.0 published 2026-11-02; repo pushed 2026-11-02
excels: Idempotent side effects outside a request layer: queue jobs; webhook and payment calls; DB writes; SDK method calls done by hand
why: Jittered backoff and abortability and per-attempt logging are easy to get subtly wrong - this is the small reviewed implementation replacing an inline while loop
when_to_use: Wrapping call sites no data layer covers - background workers and CLI network hops and non-HTTP RPC
when_not: Never stack it on top of ky or ofetch or got retry or you get double-retry storms; inside TanStack Query use its retry option; durable scheduling and dead-letter queues - a job system instead
alternatives: ky built-in retry; got built-in retry; axios-retry; exponential-backoff; p-timeout

name: pusher-channels-js
task: managed WebSocket realtime with channels and presence
what: Official Pusher Channels client: auto reconnect with history resume; subscribe and unsubscribe; private and presence channels with server-signed auth; client events; debug logging; works in browsers and Node and React Native and workers
runtime: browsers; Node; React Native; web workers - requires a Pusher app plus server-side keys
adoption: 4.4M npm dl/wk; 2.2k stars; v8.6.0 published 2026-07-23; repo pushed 2026-11-02
excels: Live features shipped quickly: typing indicators and presence and per-tenant channels and notification fan-out
why: Reconnect backoff and channel authorization and heartbeats and socket-tier scaling leave your infrastructure - the parts agents hand-roll and get wrong under load
when_to_use: You accept a metered SaaS dependency and want channels with auth and presence rather than running your own WebSocket fleet
when_not: Vendor lock with per-message pricing and an outage blast radius; self-hosted or open-protocol requirement - socket.io or Centrifugo; one-way server push - SSE is cheaper; simple polling needs none of this
alternatives: ably; supabase realtime; socket.io-client; Centrifugo; native WebSocket plus reconnecting-websocket

name: react-hook-form
what: Hook-based form state: register refs keep inputs uncontrolled so keystrokes do not re-render the tree; field arrays; watch and subscribe for selective re-rendering; built-in plus schema validation through resolvers; async validation; Controller for controlled islands
runtime: browsers React 16.8+ through 19; React Native; SSR-safe
adoption: 62.6M npm dl/wk; 44.9k stars; v7.92.0 published 2026-11-11; repo pushed 2026-11-13
excels: Large forms and multi-step wizards and any screen where a keystroke used to re-render the whole page
why: Zero re-renders per keystroke by default plus a small bundle - the standard cure for useState-per-field and onChange soup
when_to_use: Client-heavy forms needing validation and dynamic field arrays and performance; combine with a zod resolver for shared schema rules
when_not: Server Action or form-first SSR flows wanting progressive enhancement and no-JS submits - conform; typed reactive cross-field state machines and devtools - TanStack Form; a two-field login - plain useState
alternatives: TanStack Form; conform; final-form legacy; Formik legacy; controlled native inputs

name: swr
task: lightweight React data hook with cache and revalidation
what: React hooks for remote data: keyed cache; stale-while-revalidate; revalidation on interval or window focus; mutate for local cache writes; preload plus useSWRInfinite
runtime: browser React 16.11+ through 19; React Native; works with any fetcher function
adoption: 26.4M npm dl/wk; 32.5k stars; v2.5.1 published 2026-08-12; repo pushed 2026-10-16
excels: Next.js and Vercel apps plus small-to-mid React UIs that only need data-on-cache semantics
why: Delivers the core of server-state caching at a fraction of the concepts and bundle - less abstraction to learn and less to misconfigure
when_to_use: You want the smallest credible server-state layer or tight Next.js App Router behaviour and your cache rules are simple key-to-value
when_not: Dependent and parallel query orchestration; devtools inspection; cursor pagination; persisted offline cache; mutation rollback queues - TanStack Query goes deeper; one-shot calls - plain fetch or ky
alternatives: TanStack Query; RTK Query; ky plus manual state; @tanstack/react-router loaders

name: tanstack-form
what: Headless form framework on a subscribable store: field and form level sync plus async validation; dependency-aware reactive validation and error clearing; cross-field effects; form state persistence and hydration; framework adapters for react and react-native and others; first-class TypeScript inference
runtime: browsers React 17+ through 19; React Native; other frameworks via @tanstack/form-core adapters
adoption: 7.0M npm dl/wk; 6.8k stars; v1.33.5 published 2026-08-11; repo pushed 2026-11-12
excels: Forms where fields depend on each other and multi-step flows and submitting into a TanStack Query mutation with typed errors
why: Reactive derived state replaces the effect chains you would write for cross-field rules and it shares a mental model with TanStack Query
when_to_use: You already use TanStack Query and need typed cross-field or async validation or an explicit form state machine with devtools
when_not: Large legacy forms already on react-hook-form - migration cost outweighs the gains; pure server Action forms with no meaningful client state - conform; tiny forms - plain inputs plus useState
alternatives: react-hook-form; conform; final-form; zod plus custom; @xstate/react for explicit machines
tags: react; forms; type-safe; validation; state-machine; headless

name: tanstack-query
task: server-state cache and mutation sync for React
what: Hooks owning fetch plus cache plus revalidation: request dedup; stale-while-revalidate; retry with backoff; key-based invalidation; infinite queries; optimistic writes; suspense variants
runtime: browser React 18+; React Native; other frameworks via @tanstack/query-core
adoption: 84.4M npm dl/wk; 50.6k stars; v5.107.1 published 2026-11-06; repo pushed 2026-11-13
excels: List and detail screens refetched on focus or remount; paginated feeds; mutation UX with rollback across a whole app
why: Removes the useState plus useEffect loading-error-refetch trio per screen: one queryKey holds data and status in a shared cache so remounts stop hammering the API
when_to_use: React app on a REST or RPC API needing caching and revalidation and optimistic mutation writes without a GraphQL layer
when_not: Single throwaway request in an event handler or CLI script; pure WebSocket live state; normalized entity graph across many fragments - use Apollo; raw transport only - use ky or ofetch
alternatives: swr; @apollo/client; RTK Query; ky for transport; @tanstack/react-router loaders
tags: react; caching; fetch; mutation; optimistic-ui; infinite-query; retry

name: tanstack-query-persist-client
task: cache adapter persisting server state across reloads
what: Persistor bindings that write the query cache to AsyncStorage or IndexedDB or localStorage with debounce and a key allow-list and maxAge plus a hydration gate: persistQueryClient with createSyncStoragePersister or createAsyncStoragePersister
runtime: browsers; React Native; any storage driver implementing the persistor interface
excels: Offline-tolerant mobile web and React Native screens that must paint instantly on a cold start
why: The cache survives reload and app kill so first render has data - and it deletes the bespoke JSON-to-localStorage serializer with no TTL or size cap or invalidation
when_to_use: You need warm start or flaky-network UX on top of TanStack Query
when_not: Do not persist tokens or PII in clear-text storage; a general keyval store - idb-keyval or localforage; server-rendered apps must gate hydration and often need no persistence at all
alternatives: idb-keyval; localforage; swr manual cache seeding; Workbox
