name: autocannon
what: scriptable benchmarking client (connections; pipelining; workers) reporting latency percentiles and throughput; programmatic API for CI budgets; exit codes on threshold breaches
adoption: 910k/wk npm (9.0.0 published 2026-11-06) - below the mass-adoption line but the JS-native niche since k6 is not a Node package
excels: a perf budget asserted inside the test suite
why: agents hand-roll fetch for-loops and mis-measure; autocannon keeps connections warm and reports p50/p99 honestly
when_to_use: pre-merge smoke on a hot endpoint; capacity checks from Node; CI perf gates with thresholds
when_not: for multi-scenario journeys and dashboards use Grafana k6 - the npm package named k6 is a 2017 dummy stub for editor autocomplete so install k6 as a Go binary via brew or Docker and run its JS scripts outside Node; not a protocol fuzzer

name: axe-core-playwright
what: AxeBuilder injects axe-core into a Playwright page and returns rule violations with targets; include/exclude scoping; withTags for WCAG levels; disableRules
excels: catching contrast/label/aria regressions in CI
why: agents grep for alt attributes; axe is the same rule engine the browser extension runs and reports machine-checkable rule ids
when_to_use: PR gates on key routes; component-testing suites; runs tagged to wcag2a/wcag2aa
when_not: a clean run is not WCAG compliance - no keyboard-flow or reading-order judgment; false positives need triage; license is MPL-2.0 not MIT so proprietary builds may want a legal nod;jest-axe if you only test in jsdom

name: cypress
what: in-browser runner with command retry-ability; cy.intercept network stubs; cy.clock; component testing; Test Runner UI and trails
adoption: 7.1M/wk npm (16.3.0 published 2026-11-10 - active but far behind Playwright)
excels: interactive debugging of one failing test
why: the command trail with DOM snapshots beats re-running with console logs; docs and ecosystem are enormous
when_to_use: JS-only teams; existing Cypress suites; app-shell flows where authoring comfort dominates
when_not: honest limits from the Cypress docs: two origins in one test require cy.origin; cross-origin iframes unsupported; HTTPS to HTTP navigation errors; one tab per test; no WebKit; parallelization is paid on Cypress Cloud; Node-side API tests are not its job

name: faker-js-faker
what: locale-aware generators for names; emails; addresses; dates; numbers and strings with per-run seeds
excels: replacing Math.random loops with logged seeds
why: every test file re-invents randUser(); faker gives locale-correct values reproducible from a printed faker.seed()
when_to_use: fixture bodies; DB seeding; input values for unit tests; demo data
when_not: for schema-valid fake data the zod fake family is stale (zod-fixture 2.5.2 last publish 2024; @anatine/zod-mock 3.14.0 peers faker 7-9 and zod 3 only) so generate then zod.parse; for override-friendly object graphs pick factories; not for property-space coverage

name: fast-check
what: arbitraries plus generators with automatic counterexample shrinking; seeded runs; predicates and race helpers; @fast-check/vitest 0.5.0 adds test.prop and a one-time random mode
excels: shrinking a failure to the smallest readable input
why: the gem agents skip: thousands of generated cases plus a minimal counterexample instead of three guessed examples - surfaces the unicode/empty/negative/overflow bug classes
when_to_use: parsers; normalizers; currency and date math; round-trip and idempotence claims; config validation
when_not: DOM interaction flows (generated UI steps go flaky); write example tests first when the property is unclear; needs fixed seeds for deterministic CI
alternatives: jsverify (stale);hand-written example tables;@fast-check/vitest as runner glue

name: fishery
task: typed factories with overrides and sequences
what: Factory.define<T> with sequence counters; associations by composing factories; build/buildList/patch; create plus onCreate hooks for persistence
adoption: 1.43M/wk npm (2.4.0 published 2025-12-08) - niche-category-defining as the only maintained TS factory lib
excels: one place to change the shape of a User
why: agents paste makeUser() helpers per file that break on every type change; a typed factory keeps rows unique and override-friendly
when_to_use: object graphs in unit and integration tests; create() to seed a test DB; fixture-driven API tests
when_not: it knows nothing about your schema - pair with faker for values and zod or DB constraints for validity; zod-driven generators lag zod 4 (zod-fast-check 0.10.1 caps fast-check below 4)

name: jest
task: mature runner and the React Native default
what: sandboxed module registry with jest.mock hoisting; built-in snapshot and inline snapshot; jest.useFakeTimers; istanbul coverage; projects and sharding for monorepos
excels: the mocking and snapshot semantics every blog post assumes
why: most documentation and model answers are Jest-shaped; its fake timers wrap @sinonjs/fake-timers - the same engine Vitest uses - so knowledge transfers both ways
when_to_use: existing suites; React Native; CI images pinned to Node 18/20; tooling that only hooks Jest setup files
when_not: brand-new Vite or ESM-first codebases - pure ESM still needs --experimental-vm-modules plus transform config; slower cold start than Vitest on the same suite

name: msw
task: API mocking by intercepting real requests
what: one set of http/graphql handlers reused by setupServer in Node and setupWorker in the browser; res.once; passthrough; latency and network-error simulation
excels: mocks that cannot drift from the client code
why: kill the jest.mock(apiClient) layer - the real fetch runs and only the network lies
when_to_use: integration tests through axios/fetch; a shared dev mock server; error and latency paths
when_not: msw v3 is ESM-only and needs Node 22.12+ (peers vite>=6 and typescript>=5.9) so older stacks stay on v2; a single fake response is lighter with vi.mock or undici MockAgent; never inside load tests

name: pact-foundation-pact
what: consumer expectations recorded as Pact files and replayed by provider verification; the Rust reference core arrives as the @pact-foundation/pact-core dependency; matrix and CI tooling
adoption: 1.02M/wk npm (17.1.4 published 2026-09-07; needs Node 22+) - niche-category-defining; the old pact-node npm package is abandoned (last publish 2016-06 - never install it)
excels: catching provider breakage before integration tests run
why: hand-written cross-service tests either over-stub (msw) or need both services live; contracts pin the agreed interaction offline
when_to_use: multi-team microservice APIs; partner-facing endpoints; provider refactors needing a safety net
when_not: single-service apps gain little; heavyweight for internal CRUD; version pinning of the Rust core makes upgrades bumpy; docs live at docs.pact.io not the npm README
alternatives: msw for local mocks;OpenAPI or zod schema diff checks in CI;supertest for one-shot HTTP assertions

name: pixelmatch
task: pixel diff two images (pngjs is its decode pair)
what: perceptual-ish threshold diff over raw RGBA buffers; returns the mismatch count; optional highlighted diff PNG; anti-aliased pixel skipping; CLI with distinct exit codes; v8 is ESM-only and takes buffers so pngjs (7.0.0 MIT; 104.1M/wk; last publish 2023-02 - unmaintained yet ubiquitous) decodes both sides
excels: the twenty-line visual check inside a script
why: when screenshots come from outside the browser (device farms; canvas; PDF raster; design mockups) you diff them yourself and this is the standard kernel - pair with pngjs instead of hand-rolling zlib filters
when_to_use: custom visual harnesses; mobile parity checks; build-time golden image gates
when_not: in-browser page shots use Playwright toHaveScreenshot which already does capture plus compare plus masking; threshold and AA tuning is per font and OS; pngjs decode is slow on large images - use sharp or odiff-bin then

name: playwright-test
task: e2e plus component tests plus built-in visual compare
what: multi-browser runner (Chromium/Firefox/WebKit) with auto-wait web-first assertions; tracing and video; projects; expect(page).toHaveScreenshot for pixel compare with mask and animation control; toMatchAriaSnapshot; request fixture for API checks; @playwright/experimental-ct-* for component tests
excels: killing hand-rolled sleeps and flaky polling
why: auto-wait plus web-first assertions own the retry logic agents otherwise write; visual diffing is built in so a paid visual-regression vendor stays optional
when_to_use: cross-browser journeys; mobile emulation; API smoke via the request fixture; screenshot baselines on key screens
when_not: jsdom unit tests are too heavy here; component testing packages still labelled experimental and version-lagged (1.62.1 vs 1.65.0); baselines are per-OS so Linux CI must generate its own PNGs
alternatives: cypress;webdriverio;jest-image-snapshot (1.02M/wk) or reg-suit (187k/wk - last publish 2025-08) for hosted baselines

name: sinon
task: spies stubs fakes and clock outside any runner
what: standalone test doubles (spy; stub; mock; fake) plus the fake timer engine (@sinonjs/fake-timers is a direct dependency of 22.1.0); 22.x ships dual ESM and CJS entry points; HTTP faking now lives in the separate nise package (6.1.5)
adoption: 12.8M/wk npm (22.1.0 published 2026-07-20 - maintained but shrinking in share)
excels: doubles on objects you cannot module-mock
why: runner mocks are module-scoped and hoisting-sensitive; sinon fakes any live function or timer at runtime and its fake-timers package is the engine both runners ship
when_to_use: runner-less scripts and e2e setup code; legacy suites already on sinon; queue/socket/timer-heavy double choreography
when_not: new vitest/jest projects rarely need it - built-in spies and vi.mock cover most and are typed; the mock() expectation style is the criticized API - prefer stub plus explicit assertions; add nise separately for fake XHR/server since sinon dropped it

name: sinonjs-fake-timers
task: standalone time control for Date and timers
what: install() returns a clock with setSystemTime; tick; nextFrame; and advanceTimersByTimeAsync - the same engine jest and vitest wrap internally
adoption: 87.7M/wk npm (15.4.0 published 2026-05-05) - almost all transitive via @jest/fake-timers and Vitest
excels: freezing time without a test runner
why: honesty note: inside a runner you call vi.useFakeTimers or jest.useFakeTimers (both built on this exact package - Vitest pins 15.4.0) and never install it; standalone use is for runner-free libraries and scripts
when_to_use: timer-driven code tested outside a runner; deterministic clocks in demos and dev harnesses; interval and timeout assertions
when_not: mockdate (last publish 2021) should not be added for this; timezone bugs want timezone-mock not a frozen clock; faking timers while awaiting real I/O deadlocks the test

name: stryker-mutator-core
task: mutation testing - do the tests actually fail
what: generates mutants (operator flips; boundary and boolean changes) and re-runs the runner per mutant; mutation score with HTML and diff reports; incremental mode; ignore rules; TypeScript checker; jest/vitest/mocha/tap/karma/cucumber/jasmine runners
excels: exposing 100% coverage that asserts nothing
why: a surviving mutant is a missing assertion - the only JS tool that grades test quality instead of test reach
when_to_use: nightly or weekly runs on core packages; after refactoring critical logic; score trend reporting rather than a hard gate
when_not: not per-PR by default - every mutant re-runs suites so minutes become hours; flaky suites read as kills; UI-heavy code yields weak signal
alternatives: @vitest/coverage-v8 thresholds (reach not quality - the c8 provider is retired);no real JS competitor

name: supertest
task: HTTP assertions against a Node server or app
what: request(app).get(path).expect(status or body) bound to an ephemeral port; accepts http.Server or a listener function; runner-agnostic; built on superagent 10.x (10.4.2 released 2026-11-07 - both still maintained; repo now under the forwardemail org)
excels: testing the real HTTP boundary not the handler
why: agents mock req and res (node-mocks-http 2.6M/wk) and miss middleware and status codes and serialization - supertest opens a socket and speaks HTTP
when_to_use: route and controller integration tests for express/koa/plain http servers; redirect and cookie and auth flows
when_not: Fastify repos go faster and socket-free with light-my-request (22.8M/wk); against an already-listening deployment plain fetch plus runner assertions is simpler; browser-side stubbing is msw; cross-service guarantees are pact not supertest

name: testing-library-react
task: component tests written as user behavior
what: renders real components in a DOM and queries by role/label/text with automatic cleanup; built on @testing-library/dom (peer ^10) and paired with @testing-library/jest-dom for DOM matchers
excels: queries that survive markup refactors
why: agents hand-roll querySelector and class-name assertions; this goes through the accessibility tree and wires act() correctly; peer deps are NOT auto-installed so setup trips people up
when_to_use: React component and hook tests in jsdom; multi-component integration flows
when_not: pure logic needs no DOM; visual/layout claims belong to Playwright; React Native uses @testing-library/react-native; avoid assertions on styling or state internals

name: testing-library-user-event
task: realistic clicks typing and keyboard input
what: high-fidelity interaction API (click; type; paste; clear; keyboard sequences) that replays the browser event chain including pointer/focus/blur
excels: controlled inputs that behave like the browser
why: fireEvent skips focus/blur and pointer ordering so forms and pickers misbehave; agents respond with hand-written dispatchEvent loops
when_to_use: any test touching a form; keyboard shortcuts; upload and paste flows
when_not: inside Playwright browser tests (real input already); fireEvent remains the documented escape hatch for exotic edges; needs user.setup() wiring in v14

name: vitest
task: unit and integration runner for JS and TS
what: runner on Vite transforms (TS/JSX/ESM with no babel config); vi.fn spies; vi.mock module mocking; vi.useFakeTimers with vi.setSystemTime; vi.waitFor and expect.poll instead of sleeps; v8 coverage; watch and UI modes; browser mode for component tests
excels: one command for run plus coverage plus mocks in a Vite project
why: agents hand-roll babel/jest config dances and setTimeout waits; vi.waitFor owns the wait loop and the c8 provider is retired (@vitest/coverage-c8 frozen at 0.33; v8 is the default and its AST remapping matches istanbul accuracy since 3.2)
when_to_use: new TS/JS codebases; component unit tests in jsdom or happy-dom; one config for unit plus in-browser tests
when_not: Vitest 5 demands Vite 6.4+ and Node 22.12+ so Node 18/20 CI or webpack-only repos pay an upgrade first; React Native still rides the jest metro preset; jsdom/happy-dom are optional peers you must install
alternatives: jest;ava;node:test plus c8 for runner-free coverage

name: biomejs-biome
task: lint and format in one tool
what: Rust toolchain shipping formatter linter and assist for JS TS JSX JSON CSS GraphQL HTML Markdown YAML SCSS in one binary
excels: one command replaces two tools and one config file; README claims 97% Prettier compatibility and 750+ rules drawn from ESLint and typescript-eslint ecosystems
why: formatting plus linting plus import sorting in a single fast pass removes the classic prettier-versus-eslint argument
when_to_use: standard TS stack where you accept losing bespoke ESLint plugins; teams adopting a Rust toolchain for CI speed; also good as editor-time formatter
when_not: rules are largely syntax-based - Biome implements its own type inference rather than using the TypeScript compiler (oxc's comparison notes coverage is still improving) so deep type-aware rules and framework presets may not port; no JS ESLint plugin host; biomejs.dev was unreachable from this worker network so README facts come from the repo

name: changesets-cli
task: version changelog and publish for monorepos
what: files-based intent capture: humans record a changeset per PR and CI computes version bumps writes changelogs and publishes
excels: predictable multi-package versioning with human-readable CHANGELOG.md files and a version PR that batches releases
why: de-coupled from commit-message discipline - the bump decision is declared explicitly which is why library monorepos prefer it over fully automatic schemes
when_to_use: open-source or internal multi-package libraries released from CI; teams wanting release intent in the diff
when_not: not a commit-lint or hooks system: pair @commitlint/cli 21.2.4 (15.0M downloads/wk; published 2026-10-18) with husky 9.1.7 (48.8M downloads/wk; unchanged since 2024-11) and lint-staged 17.6.0 (39.8M downloads/wk) for message and pre-commit enforcement; if you want commits-derived automation use semantic-release 25.0.9 (4.1M downloads/wk) accepting a much bigger CI commitment; for raw git operations simple-git 4.0.2 (15.2M downloads/wk) beats isomorphic-git 1.44.13 (3.2M downloads/wk) unless you truly cannot shell out to a git binary
alternatives: semantic-release; standard-version? - use: release-it; nx release; lerna

name: cosmiconfig
what: searches upward for rc files and a package.json property and parses JS TS JSON and YAML into config plus source filepath
excels: the standard answer when your tool must find user config the way users expect (module name rc variants plus package.json key plus search places)
why: v10 dropped its typescript dependency in favour of Node's own type stripping so TS config files load natively; also handles JSON via plain JSON.parse and UTF-16 files
when_to_use: tools that read config from the user's project directory tree; multi-format config support without writing your own resolver
when_not: Node 22.18+ gate rules out older runtimes and type stripping rejects non-erasable syntax such as enum and namespace in config files; if config lives in one known file just import it; for environment variables use @dotenvx/dotenvx 2.38.2 (23.0M downloads/wk; BSD-3-Clause; published 2026-10-20) or Node's built-in process.loadEnvFile - dotenvx is healthy but its encryption and key model is a separate commitment

name: esbuild
what: Go single-binary that transforms TS/JSX and bundles without type checking; used as a library API or CLI
excels: raw transform and bundle latency per byte shipped; the JS API is two calls and no config file
why: speed-to-simplicity ratio is still unmatched for build scripts and one-off transforms; almost no dependencies (0 runtime deps)
when_to_use: task runner steps and file watchers; programmatic TS or JSX transforms; esoteric bundling inside your own tool
when_not: no .d.ts emission and no real plugin depth for library publishing; Vite 8 and tsdown both moved off it as the primary bundler; 0.x version numbering though the API has been stable for years
alternatives: rolldown; oxc transform; swc; sucrase; tsdown

name: eslint-prettier
what: ESLint flat-config linter with the widest rule and plugin ecosystem paired with Prettier as the opinionated formatter
langs: TypeScript; JavaScript; JSX; framework dialects via plugins
adoption: eslint 203.0M downloads/wk v10.14.0 published 2026-10-30; prettier 181.0M downloads/wk v3.10.1 published 2026-11-12
excels: the only stack where every framework-specific rule already exists (react-hooks and a11y and import and tanstack-query style presets) plus typescript-eslint type-aware rules (115.5M downloads/wk v8.72.2)
why: every framework rule set and editor integration targets ESLint first; Prettier ends formatting debates
when_to_use: default choice when rules must exist on day one; safest for editor integrations and for orgs with custom rules already written; flat config with defineConfig is settled
when_not: slowest lint path in large repos - run oxlint or biome for throughput and keep ESLint for the residual rules; formatting is a second tool and a second CI step; migration noise from .eslintrc days still lingers in older repos
alternatives: biome; oxlint + oxfmt; typescript-eslint; prettier alone for format-only

name: jscodeshift
task: codemods over JS and TS syntax trees
what: Facebook codemod runner on a printable AST (recast and ast-types) with a transform CLI and jest-style test helpers
runtime: Node 16+; flow and TS parsers bundled
excels: prints back through recast so untouched formatting survives - the difference between a reviewable codemod diff and a whole-file rewrite
why: the default for framework upgrade scripts and mechanical API renames run once across a repo; transform files are plain modules and the runner parallelises
when_to_use: repo-wide mechanical migrations; upstream project release notes that ship transforms
when_not: no type information - it matches syntax so semantic moves need ts-morph; parser coverage for newest syntax lags TypeScript releases; overkill for template scaffolding
alternatives: ts-morph; recast 0.24.3 (58.4M downloads/wk) and ast-types 0.16.3 (93.5M downloads/wk) underneath if used directly; tree-sitter 0.25.1 (4.3M downloads/wk) only for editor-grade multi-language parsing - niche in JS land

name: nx
task: monorepo build system with graph and constraints
what: project graph platform: computed dependency graph affected-only commands generators inferred tasks and enforced module boundaries
excels: the graph is the product - affected detection plus generators plus workspace rules keep many teams in one repo honest
why: only option here that actively prevents bad structure (boundaries tags; plugin package managers) and it computes task graphs instead of you declaring them
when_to_use: large multi-team monorepo with frameworks where onboarding and structure drift cost more than setup; greenfield monorepo you are willing to scaffold with nx init
when_not: heavyweight for two or three packages; the daemon and plugin surface are extra things to debug; you still need pnpm or npm under it and its own task declaration style to learn

name: oxlint
what: Rust linter on the Oxc compiler stack: 870+ rules across ESLint core typescript-eslint React Jest Vitest Import Unicorn jsx-a11y with auto-fix and ESLint config migration tooling
langs: TypeScript; JavaScript; JSX; TSX; vue svelte astro script blocks
excels: documented as 50 to 100x faster than ESLint on the project's own benchmarks and used in production by Kibana Sentry Electron Renovate PostHog and others
why: the brief called it a speed niche but verification moved it up: type-aware linting now runs on tsgo (the Go port of the TypeScript compiler) so it tracks real TS semantics - the oxc docs go as far as recommending Oxlint as the primary linter and Biome's own type inference is cited as the weaker comparison
when_to_use: large repos and CI where lint wall-clock time is the complaint; new projects wanting one fast linter; incremental adoption behind ESLint with eslint-plugin-oxlint (1.6M downloads/wk) while migrating
when_not: custom ESLint JS plugins are still alpha; a few plugin edge cases stay on ESLint; it does not format - oxfmt 0.78.0 (29.2M downloads/wk) is the companion and vite-plus 1.6.0 (5.4M downloads/wk) bundles oxlint plus oxfmt if you want one command

name: plop
what: Node CLI that prompts for inputs and renders Handlebars templates into files with pllopfile-driven generators and partials
runtime: Node 18+; handlebars and inquirer under the hood
excels: team-shared boilerplate generators with prompts plus action hooks - the cheapest way to make "add a module" one command
why: keeps conventions executable instead of documented; adopted by many large component libraries; last publish 2026-01 so alive but slow-moving
when_to_use: repo scaffolding for repeating file shapes (component plus test plus story patterns); onboarding speed
when_not: template logic gets unwieldy for anything conditional or AST-correct - use ts-morph or jscodeshift for refactors and vite-plus or nx generators for richer scaffolding; download band is the lowest here though it is the category standard
alternatives: ts-morph; jscodeshift; nx generators; hygen; @graphql-codegen/cli 8.0.0 (10.1M downloads/wk) for schema-driven codegen

name: pnpm-workspaces
what: workspace protocol and isolated strict node_modules with catalog version pinning - linking only and no orchestration
excels: honest default: workspaces plus workspace:* protocol plus catalogs solve phantom-dependency and version-drift problems with nothing to learn beyond one file
why: strict linking catches undeclared imports that npm and yarn hide; disk-efficient store; fastest install of the three managers
when_to_use: small or mid monorepo where package.json scripts plus pnpm -r already cover the pipeline; repos that need reproducible installs without a build-system vendor
when_not: no task hashing no caching no affected analysis - add turbo or nx the moment CI rebuilds everything; strict node_modules break packages expecting hoisted transitive deps (public-hoist-pattern or shamefully-hoist needed)

name: rolldown
what: JavaScript/TypeScript bundler in Rust with a Rollup-compatible plugin API and esbuild-style built-in transforms
runtime: Node 20+ via napi binaries per platform
excels: project benchmarks bundle 19k modules in 1.61s versus Rollup+esbuild at 40.10s and rspack at 4.07s while keeping the Rollup plugin API
why: listed as emerging in the brief but the evidence says shipped-and-default: 1.x stable and the single unified bundler inside Vite 8 which is why its download volume is mostly inherited from vite
when_to_use: tool authors who want an esbuild-speed bundler with a real plugin API; very large module graphs; writing a build layer that must stay compatible with Vite plugins
when_not: do not hand-configure it for an app when vite already wraps it or for a library when tsdown wraps it; webpack loader and plugin ecosystems are not portable - rspack 2.3.2 (11.5M downloads/wk) is that lane; some Rollup plugin edge cases still differ

name: shiki
what: highlighter with real grammars
excels: build-time themes; WASM runtime
why: TextMate grammar fidelity beats regex highlighters
when_to_use: code blocks anywhere
when_not: prism-class regex hacks

name: ts-morph
task: TypeScript AST transforms and typed codegen
what: named wrapper over the real TypeScript compiler API: navigate print and rewrite source files with full type and symbol information
runtime: Node 20+; ships its own ts dependency
excels: only practical way to do type-aware structural edits - move symbols across files insert imports and keep the program compiling while rewriting
why: the same author as dprint so formatting-aware output is a solved concern; strong docs site and long release history; used by codegen layers in ORMs and DI frameworks
when_to_use: typed codegen (route registries DI wiring serializers); semantic migrations where you must know a symbol's type
when_not: heavier and slower than jscodeshift for pure syntax sweeps; regenerates from the AST so comment and format fidelity is not guaranteed; requires the project's tsconfig to resolve
alternatives: js-sonnet? - use: jscodeshift; typescript compiler API directly; ast-types or recast for format-preserving JS; tree-sitter 0.25.1 (4.3M downloads/wk) for multi-language editor parsing

name: tsdown
what: rolldown-powered bundler for npm libraries - emits ESM/CJS plus .d.ts through Oxc and infers entries from package.json
runtime: Node 20+; prebuilt Rust binaries per platform
excels: dual-format library build with declarations in one fast pass and the sanctioned tsup successor (tsup's own README points here)
why: shares Rolldown and Oxc with Vite 8 so it skips the slow rollup-plugin-dts declaration path; keeps tsup's main options so migration is mechanical; weekly releases from the Rolldown team
when_to_use: new TS or JS library that must publish ESM+CJS+types; migrating an existing tsup repo; monorepos already standardised on Vite/Rolldown
when_not: still pre-1.0 so pin the exact version; not an app bundler - use vite; exotic Rollup-only plugins need a compat check; unbuild 3.6.1 (340k downloads/wk; last publish 2025-08-15) is the unjs lane but stale and unjs is prototyping obuild instead
alternatives: tsup; unbuild; vite library mode; rollup; rolldown direct

name: tsup
what: esbuild-based library bundler with rollup-plugin-dts type emission; still the most installed TS library bundler
runtime: Node 14+; Bun and Deno via esbuild compat
excels: zero-config ESM+CJS+dts with splitting and shims; enormous plugin and recipe surface on the internet
why: the pattern every TS library tutorial still shows; nothing to learn if you already used it once
when_to_use: maintaining an existing tsup build where churn is not justified; simple single-entry packages
when_not: README opens with a warning that the project is no longer actively maintained and recommends tsdown - do not start a new library on it; declaration emit is the slow step; 9.0.0 pulled in rollup as a real dependency so the bundle path is no longer pure esbuild
alternatives: tsdown; unbuild; vite library mode; rolldown directly

name: turbo
what: build system that hashes tasks and runs the workspace graph in parallel with local and remote caching
excels: task caching with almost no config - upstream package outputs are content-hashed so unchanged work is skipped
why: repo position is now explicitly agent-oriented ("the build system for coding agents") and it stays package-manager agnostic across npm pnpm and yarn
when_to_use: monorepo CI time dominated by rebuilding and retesting what did not change; teams wanting a thin orchestration layer over plain scripts
when_not: no dependency graph enforcement no generators no module boundaries - that is nx's value; single-package repos gain nothing; you still own correct task declarations and hash inputs
alternatives: nx; pnpm workspaces; plain package scripts; tnpm-style scripts

name: vite
task: app dev server and app bundling
what: frontend app dev server plus production bundler; Vite 8 collapsed esbuild (dev) and Rollup (prod) into one Rolldown pipeline
excels: the default answer for shipping a web app - instant dev server and a Rolldown build with a huge framework plugin ecosystem and a searchable plugin registry
why: Big real-world build wins are documented in the Vite 8 announcement (Linear 46s to 6s; Ramp -57%; Mercedes-Benz.io up to -38%); Node and framework teams standardised on it
when_to_use: Any browser-facing app or SPA; when you want dev server plus build plus env handling in one config
when_not: Weak for published libraries - declarations and exports maps are left to you so prefer tsdown or rollup; Vite 8 replaced the dual bundlers so check plugins and build options (compat layer auto-converts esbuild and rollupOptions); install size grew roughly 15MB (lightningcss plus rolldown)
alternatives: rolldown direct; tsdown for libs; rspack for webpack compat; postcss 8.5.32 (409M downloads/wk) is only for CSS transform plugin authors; comlink 4.4.2 (4.1M downloads/wk; last publish 2024-11-07) for worker RPC

name: arktype
task: a validator that speaks the TypeScript type system itself
what: declare types as a string DSL ('string>5' style) that both type-checks like TS and validates unknowns at runtime with its own subtype checker and morphs
excels: closest thing to a real TS subtype checker at runtime: keywords; narrowing; and inference stay 1:1 with the declared type
why: agents duplicate constraints in types and in guards; arktype keeps the constraint in one string that the compiler and the runtime both understand
when_to_use: domains with rich invariants (refinements; unions; branded-ish string formats) where you want inference not casts; validation inside shared TS libraries
when_not: DSL learning curve and dense diagnostic text on big unions; smaller adapter ecosystem than zod; inference cost on enormous types; docs outpace community answers so edge cases get little traffic

name: assert-never
task: proving to the compiler that a switch over a union is exhaustive
what: single assertNever(value: never) helper plus its type: call it in the default branch and an unhandled union member becomes a compile error; at runtime it throws on unreachable paths
excels: the whole quirk is exactly one function signature and it is already depended on at millions of installs per week
why: an added union variant otherwise compiles silently and falls through to undefined behaviour at runtime
when_to_use: plain switch or if-chains over tagged unions where you want a compile-time completeness guarantee without pulling a matching library
when_not: no pattern guards; no destructuring; no inferred extraction (that is ts-pattern); only 45 stars and last publish 1.4.0 (2024-12) so most teams inline the three-line version anyway; the thrown message is generic
alternatives: ts-pattern; local assertNever snippet; satisfies never idiom; @typescript-eslint/switch-exhaustiveness-check

name: effect
task: typed error handling + DI + schema validation as one system
what: typed runtime: Effect values carrying declared errors with retries/timeouts/structured concurrency/teardown plus Schema for parsing unknowns and Context for services
excels: expected Errors and unexpected Defects are distinct in the type; one library owns parsing; config; scheduling; and shutdown so the glue never gets written
why: replaces the framework-by-accident an agent hand-rolls: Result plumbing plus a DI container plus retry loops plus cleanup handlers
when_to_use: greenfield TS backends; workers and CLIs that can adopt a whole stack; projects where cross-cutting concerns are already re-implemented per module
when_not: it is an idiom not a utility so existing Express/Next/React code fights it; v4 (4.1.4) differs sharply from the v3 examples most models memorise; one form or one endpoint should be zod/valibot; real onboarding cost for the team
alternatives: neverthrow for Result alone; zod or valibot for schemas alone; Inversify for DI alone

name: expect-type
task: asserting an inferred type in tests instead of ts-expect-error guessing
what: expectTypeOf(x).toEqualTypeOf<T>()/toMatchTypeOf<T>() compile-time type assertions with readable mismatch output; calls erase at runtime
excels: exact type equality (not assignability) with branded-type and recursive-generic handling in a zero-dependency API
why: agents 'verify' a type change by eyeballing it; a checked-in assertion makes the intended inference a test that CI can fail
when_to_use: public library or util types you must not accidentally widen; refactors where the inference is the contract; guarding against TS built-in regressions
when_not: worthless unless CI actually runs a typecheck pass since the runtime calls do nothing; vitest 5 depends on it and re-exports its own type-test API so the install count is largely transitive rather than direct; mismatch text on deep generics is still hard to read

name: knip
task: finding unused exports; files; types and dependencies
what: dependency-graph CLI with framework-aware entrypoints and plugins; reports unused exports; types; files; unlisted and duplicate dependencies; --fix removes them
excels: one command sweeps the dead code an agent leaves behind across a monorepo including types-only exports
why: dead exports accumulate silently and later get 'reused' as the source of stale behaviour; the graph analysis is exactly the thing nobody hand-rolls
when_to_use: large or multi-package TS repos; pre-release hygiene; cleanup after a refactor or a feature-flag removal; CI as a reporting step
when_not: day-one output is loud until entrypoints; barrels; and framework files are configured; it never finds type errors since it is not a checker; --fix deletes real code so review the diff; ts-prune (0.10.3 last published 2021) is unmaintained so do not pick it instead

name: neverthrow
what: small Result and Option implementation: ok/err; andThen; map; mapErr; unwrapOr; fromThrowable and combine helpers with no runtime dependencies
excels: the whole API fits in an afternoon and forces the caller to look at the failure path in the signature
why: agents re-invent a Result type in every module; this is the same shape with chains already written
when_to_use: library and domain code that wants declared failures without adopting a framework; JS as well as TS; parsing and IO boundaries wrapped by fromThrowable
when_not: no stack traces; no retry or cancellation semantics; no structured concurrency (that is Effect); slow cadence (latest npm publish 8.2.0 in 2025-02 with repo activity through Feb 2026); boundaries still need try/catch
alternatives: effect; fp-ts TaskEither; ts-results (deprecated); plain throw with try/catch

name: ts-brand
task: branded nominal types for ids without ad-hoc intersection boilerplate
what: reusable Brand<T; U> type helper so UserId and OrderId never mix despite both being strings; with helpers to create; unwrap and rebrand values
excels: one branded alias per domain id instead of scattering '& { readonly __brand: ... }' intersections that stop matching each other
why: string ids collapsing into each other is a whole class of swapped-parameter bugs that agents hand-patch with wrappers or newtype objects
when_to_use: codebases with many primitive ids (tenant/user/order UUIDs) wanting nominal typing at zero runtime cost
when_not: no dominant package for this quirk: 427 stars and last publish 0.2.0 (2024-09) so treat adoption as verified-but-narrow; a codebase with a handful of ids is better served by a local 2-line type; if Effect or type-fest is already a dependency use their Brand/Opaque instead
alternatives: type-fest Opaque/Tagged; effect Brand; @solana/nominal-types; handmade intersection

name: ts-essentials
task: type-level object surgery (deep transforms; strict pick/omit)
what: about 95 type-only transforms: DeepPartial; DeepReadonly; DeepNullable; DeepOmit; PickKeys; StrictOmit/StrictPick; UnionToIntersection; Mutable; assert
excels: the strict-* variants reject typo'd key names that built-in Pick and Omit silently ignore; deep transforms cover API DTO shapes
why: hand-rolled DeepPartial tends to lose optional arrays and nested unions; these are versioned and tested against compiler changes
when_to_use: DTO layering (API response to form state); strict key-checked pick/omit; converting unions to intersections; API-surface types
when_not: overlaps type-fest so picking both gives two vocabularies for one job; the ts-essentials.dev docs domain did not resolve during this check - rely on the README and lib listing; type-only with no runtime guarantee

name: ts-pattern
task: exhaustive pattern matching over discriminated unions
what: match(value).with(pattern; handler).exhaustive() with compile-time completeness checking; P.* guards for arrays; objects; unions; predicates and extraction
excels: the compiler refuses to let a new union case go unhandled and destructuring inside the pattern stays inferred
why: if/else chains over tagged unions lose exhaustiveness the moment someone adds a variant; this turns that into a build error
when_to_use: redux/reducer style state machines; event and message handling; any switch that must grow safely; nested discriminated unions with guards
when_not: overkill for two branches; plain switch plus assertNever is cheaper to read; deep structural scans cost real time in hot loops; very large match chains slow inference
alternatives: assert-never; native switch with satisfies never; @typescript-eslint/switch-exhaustiveness-check

name: ts-reset
task: repairing TypeScript's own wrong built-in typings
what: type-only import that overrides lib definitions: JSON.parse and Response.json() return unknown; Array.filter(Boolean) narrows properly; includes() accepts readonly arrays; localStorage/sessionStorage reads typed
excels: one import deletes the three most copy-pasted TS gotcha snippets from a codebase
why: these defects are TypeScript library bugs not app bugs so fixing them per-callsite repeats the same workaround forever
when_to_use: projects that want unknown-by-default JSON and ergonomic filter behaviour without touching every file; new TS apps starting clean
when_not: no release since 2024-09 (0.6.1) and TypeScript 5.5+ infers type predicates natively which already kills the filter case; global lib overrides confuse readers and can collide with other @types patches; needs a reset.d.ts per tsconfig project
alternatives: upgraded TypeScript itself; type-fest; per-callsite narrowing; eslint rules

name: type-fest
task: named utility types instead of hand-rolled mapped-type gymnastics
what: 295 type-only utilities: Simplify; Merge/MergeDeep; PartialDeep; Exact; Opaque/Tagged (branded types); Jsonify; RequireAtLeastOne; IsUnion; UnknownRecord; literal-case transforms
excels: the awkward corners (deep partials; deep readonly; JSON round-trip types; opaque/branded types) already have their edge cases debugged
why: agents write a broken 12-line mapped type per project for PartialDeep or Merge; these are the same names with tests attached
when_to_use: any TS codebase needing deep type transforms; branded ids via Opaque/Tagged; expressing a type whose runtime shape is JSON; intersection-exclusion
when_not: zero runtime so nothing validates a value; some utilities are expensive on giant unions; majors rename and move utilities between releases; check native TS built-ins before importing a fifth helper

name: typebox
task: JSON Schema authored in TypeScript and compiled into a validator
what: schema builder whose types ARE JSON Schema: Type/infer plus Value.Compile/TypeCompiler for AOT validation; formats; references; and strict mutation modes
excels: validation and wire-format schema are literally the same artifact; compiled validators are among the fastest on Node
why: hand-writing JSON Schema by hand then casting to TS twice is the classic drift bug; TypeBox makes one definition serve both
when_to_use: HTTP frameworks (Elysia; Fastify) and MCP/OpenAPI tool definitions; needing a machine-readable schema on the wire; performance-sensitive validation
when_not: 0.x forever: breaking changes between minors and no 1.0 contract; verbose versus zod for plain forms; type-level narrowing ergonomics weaker; docs split between site and README
alternatives: typia; zod; arktype; ajv directly; json-schema-to-ts

name: typia
task: compiling a TS type annotation into a runtime validator
what: transform that reads TypeScript type annotations and emits real code for assert()/is()/validate()/shallow() guards; typed JSON stringify+parse; protobuf codecs; random generators; and LLM function-call schemas
excels: one source of truth: the annotation IS the validator and the wire format; generated code beats interpreted validators on throughput
why: hand-written guards and duplicated schema literals drift from the interface they describe; typia pays the cost once at build time
when_to_use: v15 tracks current TypeScript (docs cover TypeScript 7): TS-only services with typed DTOs everywhere; hot validation paths; needing validation + JSON Schema + protobuf + AI tool schemas from one type
when_not: requires a compiler transform (typia CLI or ts-patch) so plain tsc or bundler-only pipelines break; cannot see interface merging or unresolvable types; its own tag/format DSL; emitted errors need mapping to user-facing copy; useless from plain JS

name: valibot
task: bundle-cheap runtime validation of unknown data
what: function-per-check schema library: schema/object/pipe with standalone actions so every validator is an individually tree-shakeable import; infers types; returns typed result or exception
excels: per-export tree shaking keeps client bundles small while still giving full TS inference
why: hand-rolled validators are usually written because zod's bundle or API feels heavy; valibot solves the size half without giving up inference
when_to_use: frontend and edge bundles where schema weight matters; env and API validation with readable pipe composition; projects wanting standard-schema compatibility
when_not: v1 is a rewrite so 0.x snippets online mislead; adapter and recipe ecosystem thinner than zod; deeply nested objects get noisy in pipe style; still interpreted at runtime

name: zod
task: runtime validation of unknown input with its TS type inferred in one place
what: schema description language that infers the static type from the schema and parses unknown data into typed results with structured issues
excels: the default: standard-schema alignment and JSON Schema interop in v4 mean OpenAPI/tRPC/ORM/MCP adapters already exist for everything
why: one declaration yields type; parse; coercion; error message; and generated schema instead of four artifacts that disagree
when_to_use: API bodies; env; query params; form payloads; LLM structured output; anywhere an agent would otherwise write if (typeof x !== 'string') throw
when_not: two sources of truth when the interface is already written elsewhere (typia/arktype fit better); v3 inference was slow on deep types and v4 moved APIs again; interpreted parse cost shows in hot loops; error copy needs localising before it reaches users

name: ag-grid-community
what: batteries-included grid with virtualization; cell editing; column panel; themes and clipboard
adoption: 5.4M npm dl/wk; 15.7k stars; v36.3.0 published 2026-11-04; repo pushed 2026-11-13
excels: hundreds of thousands of rows with row and column virtualization plus editing out of the box
why: their own feature-split page confirms the free MIT bundle covers sorting; filtering; pagination; cell renderers; theming; a11y and virtualization - the parts everyone else charges for
when_to_use: internal tools where the grid is the product: back-office; financial; analyst workbenches
when_not: the features people ask for next (Server-Side Row Model; pivoting; row grouping; range selection; Excel export; master/detail; tool panels) need a paid per-developer Enterprise licence; bundle weight and API surface swamp a simple orders list
alternatives: @tanstack/react-table for headless control; @mui/x-data-grid; ag-grid-enterprise modules; glide-data-grid (678k dl/wk; MIT canvas-rendered grid)

name: canvas-confetti
what: tiny promise-based confetti API drawing on a self-managing canvas overlay
adoption: 9.8M npm dl/wk; 12.9k stars; v1.9.4 published 2025-10-25; repo pushed 2025-10-25
excels: one-call burst with shapes; gravity; colours and origin that disposes of its own canvas
why: DIY confetti is a rAF particle loop plus a canvas that leaks - this is the 1.6KB version of that weekend project
when_to_use: onboarding complete; payment success; streak and gamification moments with a bounded scope of delight
when_not: continuous particle systems or game physics want a real renderer such as pixi.js; always gate it behind prefers-reduced-motion
alternatives: react-confetti (same engine wrapped); CSS sparkle animations; pixi.js

name: copy-to-clipboard
what: one-call copy helper that restores the text selection and falls back to execCommand
adoption: 14.5M npm dl/wk; 1.4k stars; v4.0.2 published 2026-04-24; repo pushed 2026-08-05
excels: being the honest exception where zero dependencies is the right answer
why: navigator.clipboard.writeText(text) works everywhere that matters and a temporary Copied flag is five lines - the residual value is insecure-context fallback and not clobbering the current selection
when_to_use: a copy button that must work on http/intranet pages or inside an iframe lacking clipboard-write permission
when_not: do not install it merely to copy a string; no wrapper copies images or files (that is ClipboardItem) and permission-policy plus user-gesture rules apply either way
alternatives: navigator.clipboard built-in; react-copy-to-clipboard (2.56M dl/wk; legacy class wrapper); use-clipboard-copy (109k dl/wk)

name: embla-carousel-react
what: drag carousel engine with snap points plus thin React/Vue/Svelte bindings
runtime: browser; framework-agnostic core with a react binding
adoption: 27.1M npm dl/wk for the react binding; 29.4M dl/wk core; 8.5k stars; v8.6.0 published 2025-04-04; repo pushed 2026-11-01
excels: predictable snap behaviour that survives fractional widths and window resizes
why: DIY sliders fail on the first odd device: pointer capture; momentum; re-init on resize; RTL; and loop mode are all already solved
when_to_use: product galleries; testimonial rotators; onboarding swipes needing real touch physics
when_not: need coverflow/cube/fade effects or a media viewer with thumbnail pagination - Swiper (5.2M dl/wk; 41.9k stars) ships those; autoplay is a separate plugin not a builtin
alternatives: swiper; keen-slider; pure CSS scroll-snap for dumb scrollers

name: floating-ui-react
task: tooltips popovers dropdowns and context menus
what: positioning engine plus interaction hooks (useHover; useFocus; useDismiss; useRole) with arrow and flip
adoption: 33.7M npm dl/wk; 32.8k stars; v0.27.20 published 2026-07-11; repo pushed 2026-11-12
excels: collision-aware placement across scrolling ancestors with dismiss and focus guards
why: hand-built tooltips clip off-screen and detach on scroll while right-click menus forget the anchor coordinates and focus restore - this is the geometry layer everyone rebuilds badly
when_to_use: custom tooltips; select and combobox popovers; canvas/editor context menus anchored to pointer coordinates
when_not: if the app already uses Radix; base-ui or Ariakit menus/popovers then those wrap this engine - do not stack two positioning systems; semantics and focus order remain yours
alternatives: tippy.js (8.19M dl/wk but the repo is ARCHIVED with 6.3.7 published 2021-11-10 - avoid for new work); @floating-ui/dom for vanilla; radix-ui; cmdk for palettes

name: howler
task: audio playback for UI and games
what: Web Audio/HTML5 audio abstraction with sprites; fading; pools and spatial panning
runtime: browser; also usable in hybrid apps
adoption: 1.37M npm dl/wk; 25.4k stars; v2.2.4 published 2023-09-19; repo pushed 2025-11-23
excels: iOS unlock/autoplay handling plus sprite mapping and multi-voice pooling in one call
why: raw new Audio() gives no fade; no sprite table; no format fallback; and the mobile unlock behaviour has to be rediscovered per device
when_to_use: sound effects; UI feedback sounds; background music with crossfades; overlapping game voices
when_not: project is effectively maintenance-only (last release 2023) though stable; synthesis and sample-accurate sequencing belong to Tone.js (309k dl/wk; 14.9k stars); one click sound needs only the native audio element
alternatives: Web Audio API directly; tone; pixi-sound; native audio element

name: qrcode-react
what: SVG and canvas QR component with error-correction level; margin and logo-overlay props
adoption: 14.4M npm dl/wk; 4.3k stars; v4.2.0 published 2024-12-11; repo pushed 2026-11-13
excels: renders as a real SVG node so CSS sizing stays crisp at print resolution
why: encoder plus Reed-Solomon level and module matrix is exactly what silently produces unscannable codes when hand-rolled
when_to_use: 2FA provisioning URIs; share links; ticket and check-in codes inside a React tree
when_not: server-side or PDF/PNG generation - the engine package qrcode (41.0M dl/wk; 8.2k stars; last published 1.5.4 on 2024-08-05) covers canvas/terminal/node; dense payloads with a logo overlay break scannability so keep level H and test a real scan
alternatives: qrcode; react-qr-code; qr-code-styling for logos and rounded modules; canvas output from the qrcode engine

name: react-arborist
what: virtualized tree with drag-and-drop re-parenting; inline rename; multi-select and keyboard navigation
adoption: 860k npm dl/wk - niche but category-defining and the only actively maintained option; 3.7k stars; v4.0.1 published 2026-10-11; repo pushed 2026-11-02
excels: the VSCode/Finder/Figma-layers interaction set is already built: indent guides; drop onto folders; ARIA attributes; open/close state
why: recursive nested-ul trees die at a few thousand nodes and drag re-parenting is index math nobody gets right twice
when_to_use: file explorers; category trees; design-tool layers panels; org charts
when_not: a flat 20-item category list belongs in a plain nested ul; you own data mutation and the drag payload semantics; single-maintainer niche so budget for a fork
alternatives: @headless-tree; react-complex-tree; building on @tanstack/react-virtual; rc-tree from Ant Design
